specs.title: Explicit isolated browser modes
specs.contract: Trusted startup browser.mode requires headless or headed, with headless and browser.viewer=false as production defaults. Invalid or missing modes/viewer settings fail without fallback; a viewer requires headed mode. Headed Chrome uses container-local Xvfb UNIX sockets, with no host display/device/socket mount. Headless launches no display/viewer. Both modes preserve owned disposable browser lifecycle, required sandbox/native download policy, sole anonymous default context, private CDP and verified configured main-window contents/global scale.

specs.title: Local session-authenticated browser viewer
specs.contract: Existing browser container optionally serves packaged noVNC through websockify and container-local x11vnc UNIX socket. Docker publishes only configured viewer TCP port on 127.0.0.1 through existing firewall service and its dedicated viewer bridge; restricted browser bridge stays internal and CDP remains unpublished. Enabled viewer accepts only viewer-bridge host-gateway initiated traffic and established replies, preserving other browser network denials. HTTP assets and WebSocket require fresh per-browser-run high-entropy Basic authentication; Host and supplied Origin must name local viewer. Trusted BrowserRun.viewer_access returns URL/login only after owned readiness, separately from Scout environment/model tools. Session secret exists only in browser tmpfs, never process arguments, readiness or persisted logs; credentials rotate on each fresh run. Disabled viewer starts no listener or credential. Closing viewer connection leaves browser and mission running; normal owned cleanup removes display/viewer too. No fifth service, custom viewer framework, automatic reconnect/recovery or public/LAN/CDP access is added.

specs.title: Trusted human input and ordinary Scout actions
specs.contract: Authenticated noVNC lets a trusted operator see headed Chrome and click/type through native VNC input. Scout actions use the ordinary run-owned browser executor without independent review. Manual changes can make an observed original reference stale, which must reject before proposed effect; there is no pending approval or cross-review context baseline. Controlled-page tests exercise actual noVNC canvas, mouse and keys, page effects and continued browser use after viewer closure. No human-input interception, replacement selection, automatic action replay or deferred tab-closure/crash behavior is introduced.

specs.title: Clean browser identity
specs.contract: Every mission uses a dedicated Hermes home and an ephemeral anonymous Signal Scout browser identity with no real profile, arbitrary external CDP attachment, personal history, personal cookies, personal account, or inherited extensions. Remote CDP is permitted only for the freshly created, exactly run-owned isolated browser container under SR_004/SR_005, not an independently supplied endpoint. Mission start fails if runtime cannot attest this policy, and report records attested browser identity. Protection-only container ownership does not complete this mission contract.

specs.title: Read-only research intent and restricted tool scope
specs.contract: Milestone1 retains a whole-mission default-deny tool policy and immutable operating boundaries. The browser slice uses explicit allowed/blocked actions and native adapter routing under BR_001-BR_005; configured research exposes only browser_scout. Main-agent research instructions discourage purchases, account creation, posting, messaging, uploads and account changes and treat webpage instructions as untrusted data. These directions do not independently classify or enforce site effects after reviewer retirement. Broader mission policy, report attestation, account integration, extraction activation and whole-mission audit requirements remain incomplete.

specs.title: Untrusted content boundary
specs.contract: Signal Scout treats webpage text, captions, transcripts, comments, metadata, downloaded content, and stored excerpts as untrusted research data. Hermes web and browser result framing is preserved, delimiter tokens inside attacker content are neutralized, and evidence returned during resume is independently framed. Source content cannot mutate the immutable mission, tool policy, safety ceiling, security policy, or output destination.

specs.title: Media artifact quarantine
specs.contract: Media retrieved for analysis is accepted only when its detected type and size satisfy the mission policy, stored in a mission-specific quarantine, and passed only to declared analyzers. Signal Scout never executes a retrieved artifact and reports rejected, mismatched, or oversized content.

specs.title: Browser local network isolation
specs.contract: Scout's deterministic public-web browser harness validates raw HTTP(S) syntax and absence of embedded credentials, without duplicate DNS/IP policy. Proxy owns fresh DNS resolution, every-answer IP classification, numeric destination pinning, and actual connected-peer verification. Browser web traffic permits only public HTTP:80 and HTTPS:443; DNS failure, loopback, unspecified, multicast, link-local, private/local, reserved, transition-to-private, and metadata IPv4/IPv6 addresses are denied. Redirects and DNS rebinding cannot bypass checks. Forbidden main URLs/redirects fail navigation; forbidden embedded/background requests fail individually while public content can load. Sanitized best-effort logging never loosens enforcement. Browser namespace firewall denies direct and DNS bypass; proxy admits only configured browser source address. Browser cannot initiate toward Hermes, host/LAN/metadata or direct Internet. Hermes connects directly without this Scout-specific egress restriction or proxy configuration; no Hermes host/LAN isolation is claimed. TLS stays end-to-end verified. Owned remote control exceptions are not webpage access (SR_002). Harness exposes no model browser tool and does not complete mission policy.

specs.title: Mandatory attested isolated Chromium sandbox
specs.contract: Image pins existing Hermes-supported native agent-browser on Hermes side and Chromium on isolated browser side. Trusted launcher starts one newly owned Chromium with mandatory sandbox/proxy flags and fresh anonymous temporary profile/XDG storage, never a real profile, cloud/local fallback or TLS bypass. Launcher proves child owns loopback listener before relay readiness. Existing native Hermes remote-CDP path connects only to checked run-owned endpoint. Before untrusted navigation actual chrome://sandbox must show PID namespaces, network namespaces and seccomp-BPF active; unavailable sandbox fails without no-sandbox fallback. Tests make no model calls; browser and Hermes have separate PID/mount/network namespaces.

specs.title: Narrow owned browser management exceptions
specs.contract: Hermes connects directly to configured private browser relay in its own unrestricted-by-Scout namespace. Browser namespace firewall permits only configured Hermes source into relay, narrow loopback launcher/relay-to-Chromium CDP control and necessary replies in addition to browser proxy access. Relay admits configured Hermes source IP only and forwards solely to newly owned child's loopback listener; child exit closes relay. No host-published CDP port, broad browser loopback allowance or private-web exception; optional authenticated localhost viewer transport is separately owned under SR_012. Endpoint host/port/browser path and discovery are checked; redirects, wrong ownership and stale paths fail. Network/source-IP checks are not cryptographic authentication and do not protect against compromised trusted controller/browser. Ordinary page HTTP, WebSocket, frame, image and fetch traffic remains proxy-forced, including loopback; proxy rejects raw CDP and relay even with known active WebSocket paths. Authorized native controller remains usable without Hermes proxy environment settings.

specs.title: Persistent best-effort protection event logs
specs.contract: Scout Python events reuse native Hermes logging. Native Hermes diagnostics preserve logger names, formatted messages, session context and exception details under Hermes native secret redaction instead of being replaced by generic event classes. Native diagnostics can retain URLs and error context; there is no blanket promise that all sensitive or webpage content is removed. Proxy and browser firewall emit fixed operational/rejection events to distinct proxy.log and firewall.log files in existing dedicated log volume. Renamed firewall appends to existing firewall.log, which can contain historical Hermes-firewall events; historical browser-firewall.log files and backups remain untouched. No migration or wiping occurs. Defaults are 5 MiB/file and three backups including native errors; validated configuration controls size/backups/verbosity. Scout protection events retain timestamp, level, component and allowlisted event class. Scout event producers do not interpolate raw browser/CDP arguments/results, screenshots, bodies, cookies, credentials, secret configuration or provider exceptions. Open/write/rotation failures attempt fixed diagnostics without stopping browsing or weakening enforcement; no acknowledgment/universal monitor. Logs survive ordinary replacement while volume remains, not tamper-proof/disaster recovery. Browser has no persistent log mount and Scout Docker output is not retained. Browser diagnostics use bounded output collection by the trusted host under SR_023 and owned container-state capture under SR_024, without giving the browser access to shared logs or authentication. Mission audit/report remains incomplete.

specs.title: Isolated browser container boundary
specs.contract: Trusted host creates browser separately from credential-bearing Hermes: no shared PID/mount/network namespace, Hermes runtime, auth/research/log mounts, host folders other than the sole read-only operating-config file allowed by BT_006, Docker socket or writable shared artifact mount. Browser is non-root, readonly, capability-free, no-new-privileges and actually sandboxed with anonymous bounded temporary storage. Compose owns 2,000,000,000-byte memory and equal memory+swap, no CPU quota, PID512 and bounded tmpfs; changed resource configuration reaches actual containers. Private fixed-destination control relay is bound to exact newly created container/run and owned Chromium listener. Wrong ownership, discovery redirect, wrong/stale endpoint, unavailable sandbox or control startup fail safely without adopting/replacing browser. Network/source checks and live positive-control tests enforce boundary; no claim of immunity to browser/kernel/host compromise.

specs.title: Disposable single-run browser lifecycle
specs.contract: One trusted host lifecycle owns one active run and is reused by deterministic smoke/tests. Each run creates new browser container/process and anonymous temporary profile; second claimant or leftover container is rejected without disturbing/adopting first. Multiple tabs may exist inside run. Normal end or surfaced fatal failure removes only exact owned container and temporary state, retaining helpers, auth/log volumes and images. If Docker creates the current attempt but cannot start it, cleanup resolves exact attempted name/project/service/run ownership and verifies full ID before removal; foreign collisions remain untouched. Browser child exit closes relay; stale/unavailable control, observed native action-driver transport loss even with healthy HTTP discovery, and control-command timeout are terminal, never browser replacement, mission restart, arbitrary attachment or local/cloud fallback. Ordinary navigation denial is not itself transport loss. Navigation-specific page-load failure may follow AG_008 only while the same owned browser remains controllable and observable; other command/lifecycle failures remain terminal. Startup/local-control/shutdown/smoke bounds are consumed from validated trusted startup settings; host stop deadline allows configured shutdown grace plus bounded Docker overhead, including supported grace above 60 seconds. Existing auxiliary supervisor reconnect is not browser replacement; reconnect/degraded-monitoring policy remains deferred. If Hermes/launcher/host disappears, independent teardown is not guaranteed and requires deliberate operator inspection/cleanup; no watchdog, recovery daemon or scavenging is implemented.

specs.title: Persistent native browser download denial
specs.contract: Pinned Chrome for Testing loads root-owned/read-only /etc/opt/chrome_for_testing/policies/managed/scout.json with mandatory DownloadRestrictions: 3. Before readiness launcher verifies Chrome's validated native policy model reports value 3, mandatory/machine/platform and no error, ignored, warning, conflict or superseded policy. Native policy persists after bounded startup CDP closes, without a download override or policy-only run-lived connection. Real attachment, redirected attachment and generated-blob attempts in initial/new tabs and separate popups emit attempted-download and canceled-progress events and save no file after startup disconnect. Controlled transient policy-free images prove real attachment/redirect downloads enter native progress, then native UI cancels before payload. Ordinary HTML, image, audio and video loading remains available. Native policy blocks ordinary webpage downloads, not Save Page or print-to-PDF. No allow toggle, custom download filter or download destination is introduced. Sole fresh anonymous default context remains supported; arbitrary trusted CDP remains trusted outside the model-facing gate under AG_001–AG_007.

specs.title: Required canonical window and scale configuration
specs.contract: Existing trusted startup browser.viewport is the sole source for width, height and device_scale_factor; supplied configuration is 1280 by 720 CSS pixels and scale 1. Width and height must be positive CDP signed integers; scale must be finite, positive and numeric, never boolean. Missing values, invalid values and unknown viewport keys fail explicitly without alternate defaults. Changing startup configuration and its consistency digest reaches actual Chromium main-window contents and browser-wide device scale, not only launch arguments.

specs.title: Verified main-window contents and browser-wide scale
specs.contract: Launcher sets initial normal main-window contents with Browser.setContentsSize and browser-wide --force-device-scale-factor. Before readiness actual innerWidth, innerHeight and devicePixelRatio must match validated configuration; --window-size alone is not proof. Real viewport-only PNG captures match configured CSS dimensions multiplied by device scale. No per-tab emulation, debugger pause, screenshot cropping/full-page sizing or continuous geometry guard is implemented; unsupported actual sizing fails startup instead of falling back.

specs.title: Shared normal-tab sizing with untouched popup windows
specs.contract: Ordinary native new tabs share configured main-window identity, actual content dimensions, viewport-only capture size and browser-wide scale. Separate popup windows retain their own requested/native content size while sharing default context, mandatory download denial, network protections and browser-wide scale. Launcher does not initialize, activate or resize later targets. Native selected-tab behavior and tab-closure recovery remain deferred. No fixed viewport for every window or pre-page-execution viewport-ordering guarantee is claimed.

specs.title: Startup safeguard failures and owned cleanup
specs.contract: Missing, malformed, invalid or unapplied native download policy and main-window setup failure prevent readiness and clean the exact owned browser through existing lifecycle. Validated control_connect_timeout bounds startup CDP opening, commands and closing; startup_timeout bounds native policy observation and actual window-size verification. Launcher restores sole initial about:blank page and closes startup CDP before readiness; native policy remains effective, with no policy-only run-lived connection, keepalive or policy-disconnect watcher. A canceled download is successful enforcement and leaves healthy browser usable, not a machinery failure. Ordinary driver transport-loss, child-exit and fatal-cleanup contracts remain unchanged; no reconnect, replacement or watchdog is added. Owned cleanup retains helper state, auth/log volumes and existing ownership checks.

specs.title: Compact snapshots and immutable exact references
specs.contract: Scout-owned snapshot lists compact accessibility role/name text and monotonic @s refs for an explicit CDP page target ID, never full HTML/DOM. Private refs bind original browser node, frame, target and document lifetime. Same node can retain its ref across snapshots; existing refs never bind another node or substitute role/name lookalikes. Same-origin and cross-origin iframe nodes retain their exact frame and CDP target identities. Native agent-browser and Hermes core remain unchanged.

specs.title: Current target and keyboard-focus resolution
specs.contract: Click and type resolve the original observed node in the selected tab, reveal it with ordinary scrolling and compute its current interaction point. Keypress resolves actual current focus, including same-origin and cross-origin frames and closed author shadow roots, and permits page-level keys without inventing an element. Resolution rejects stale required nodes or focus and performs no proposed click, text replacement or keypress. Optional activity describes progress only. No screenshot, semantic form packet or approval baseline is prepared.

specs.title: Ordinary original-target and focus verification
specs.contract: Before an input effect, verify the original reference still identifies its original tab, frame, document and node, and verify actual required typing or keyboard focus. Replaced or detached original targets reject without substitution or proposed effect; healthy browsing can continue from a fresh observation. No label or role fallback, target replacement or action replay occurs. There is no pre-approval versus post-approval comparison of page titles, link/form destinations, accessibility semantics or unrelated context. Current checks do not promise atomic page or server effects.

specs.title: Visible unobstructed current interaction point
specs.contract: Compute the interaction point from current original-node geometry, including iframe clipping and coordinate projection, and verify viewport visibility and hit target. Same-node movement remains valid when its current point is visible and unobstructed; the whole element need not fit the viewport. Hidden or covered targets reject without proposed effect while healthy browsing continues. No forced interaction, full-page screenshot fallback or pixel comparison is added.

specs.title: Required ordinary browser machinery failures
specs.contract: Required ordinary inspection, explicitly requested capture, unknown protocol or control-transport failure marks the Browser unusable and produces a sanitized fatal result for existing owned teardown. Expected stale, detached, hidden, covered or unavailable required targets instead reject before proposed effect and allow healthy continuation. Known unrelated iframe loss follows AE_007. Existing command timeout, ownership and teardown apply without a reviewer, automatic input replay or browser replacement. Preserve helper state and auth/log volumes.

specs.title: Partial frame inspection and unavailable-target recovery
specs.contract: Known missing or detached iframe responses stop traversal of that unavailable branch while preserving inspectable branches. Successful snapshots and ordinary browser observations disclose incomplete inspection through code-owned metadata or notice. If the original requested target, required frame ancestry, actual keyboard focus or required current identity/hit point cannot be verified, reject that proposal without effect or replacement and permit healthy continuation. Omission state stays local to its scan and cannot contaminate another action. Unknown errors and owned-control transport failures remain fatal. No reviewer packet, approval or screenshot is required for ordinary actions; explicit screenshots and independent network/download protections remain.

specs.title: Closed requests and explicit action permissions
specs.contract: Accept only implemented browser actions with their exact action-specific string arguments and optional string activity. Validate URL syntax, reference grammar, keys, scroll direction and selected-tab arguments before effect. Trusted action_permissions permits only allowed or blocked; missing action entries remain blocked and unknown actions or modes fail. No reviewer, policy, browser identity, arbitrary selector, JavaScript executor or alternate tool route can be supplied by the model. Return recoverable sanitized rejection for malformed or blocked proposals without effect.

specs.title: Current exact execution and native interaction semantics
specs.contract: Execute each valid allowed proposal once through the run-owned selected Browser after ordinary current target resolution. Click uses current unobstructed projected coordinates of its original observed node; type validates the exact editable target, focuses it, replaces contents and verifies exact focus around native insertion. Keypress uses actual current focus and native browser key-down/key-up semantics. Original-node movement may be resolved without reviewer equivalence checks. No pre-action screenshot or auxiliary model call is required. Preserve native download denial while controlled ordinary web and media remain usable.

specs.title: Reject stale original targets before effects
specs.contract: Original references cannot silently rebind to replacement or lookalike nodes, another document, frame or tab. Expected unavailable, stale, hidden or covered required targets and unavailable required keyboard focus reject before effect and allow later healthy observation. Type and keys preserve ordinary current focus checks. Semantic differences from an earlier screenshot, label, form or approval are not a separate rejection condition because no reviewer approval exists. No automatic action replay or target substitution occurs.

specs.title: Selected-page and ordinary browser controls
specs.contract: Back, scroll, snapshots, explicit screenshots, image observations, tab listing, explicit existing-tab switching and close use the same run-owned browser and trusted allowed/blocked map as other actions. No action is classified as a review exemption. Listing and switching do not create or select replacement tabs implicitly. Preserve native scroll direction, selected-page feedback, shared browser protections and close revocation; introduce no new selected-tab closure or browser replacement behavior.

specs.title: Complete truthful outcomes and fresh applicable observations
specs.contract: Every dispatch returns a truthful gate status, fixed sanitized reason or null, truthful execution_started and dictionary data. A proposal rejected before any execution has false execution_started and no proposed effect. Started means effect/read dispatch began, not proof of server effects; post-dispatch or required observation machinery failure is fatal with true. Ordinary navigation-load failure is distinguished from machinery failure under AG_008 and never misreported as successful destination loading. Successful click/navigation/type/key/back/scroll/switch returns fresh compact AX snapshot and exact selected target_id, without automatic main-agent screenshot. Completed native download cancellation is successful enforcement: success with true execution_started, fresh selected-page AX and healthy continuation, not a claim that destination loaded or machinery-loss recovery. Explicit screenshot returns full native viewport PNG bytes/MIME in memory. Tabs/images return actual observations, close returns close result. AG_008 owns navigation-aware observations using an independent short observation deadline and the matching initial-document DOMContentLoaded event instead of a mandatory load-event wait. Navigation observations include truthful readiness and configured-deadline information for the main agent; they do not promise all media, application data or future updates are ready. SR_022 keeps raw diagnostic exceptions and protocol payloads out of model-facing results.

specs.title: Terminal browser failure and native hard stop
specs.contract: Required ordinary inspection, explicit capture, control, execution or observation machinery failure makes the gate terminal and closes its Browser. Native interruption, closed binding, failed Browser and control-route changes prevent later dispatch. Adapter invokes the original bound native hard-stop callback once, skips later effects and model turns, and allows exact host-owned cleanup. Ordinary navigation recovery is bounded by AG_008. No review verdict, review timeout, auxiliary retry, queue, watchdog, broad recovery or browser replacement remains.

specs.title: Trusted operating policy and private execution state
specs.contract: Trusted startup action_permissions supports only implemented actions with allowed or blocked values; missing permissions remain blocked. Required positive integer scroll_pixels supplies native scrolling. Gate copies trusted permissions at construction and copies external requests before work; model inputs cannot alter operating policy. Private target bindings, frame scans and copied request payloads are not copied into returned results or separate archives. Ordinary observed AX values, including typed text, intentionally reach main context; native diagnostics retain their existing redaction and retention behavior. No review packet, safety-model configuration, review mode or policy-file dependency remains.

specs.title: Early navigation observations and bounded error recovery
specs.contract: Explicit URL navigation and back observe the actual selected document until its matching DOMContentLoaded event or a configurable browser.observation_timeout, initially 5 seconds, whichever occurs first. The observation allowance starts after the corresponding browser command acknowledgment, and is not restarted by each unrelated event or redirect. Snapshot capture and other browser commands have their own control deadlines; 5 seconds is not a guaranteed total tool duration. browser.command_timeout remains the separate configured command-response deadline, initially 60 seconds. A late or missing load event alone does not delay observation until that deadline. Readiness events are bound to the actual selected tab, frame and document loader, including redirects; stale, child-frame or other-session events cannot establish readiness for the current destination. Clicks and keypresses also observe navigation when it results from their single execution, using the same readiness/deadline policy without replaying the already-executed input. Non-navigation interactions such as opening a dropdown return fresh current-page observations without waiting for a new DOMContentLoaded event or consuming the full navigation allowance. Required browser.interaction_observation_timeout initially 0.25 seconds bounds ordinary interaction observation; it cannot guarantee detection of every future delayed navigation. Both observation settings require finite positive numeric values up to 120 seconds, reject booleans, and require the interaction interval no greater than the document allowance. Subsequent actions retain ordinary original-document/node and current-focus checks. Same-document URL/content changes do not require a new document readiness event. On observation deadline with healthy owned control and capturable page evidence, return a nonfatal incomplete result with execution_started true, the verified current compact AX snapshot, exact selected target identity, actual observed URL, and a sanitized explicit reason identifying the observation deadline and configured wait duration. Distinguish a still-pending destination from the actually observed document; never call the previous document or about:blank a successfully loaded destination. Report initial-document readiness truthfully without claiming all images, async application content or later requests are ready. Return the first timeout observation without automatic reload, repeated input, another capture solely for retry, or an auxiliary safety-model call. The main agent chooses a later observation, an explicitly requested retry through the normal gate, another URL or a blocked-page report; no cross-turn timeout counter or automatic mission stop after a number of such observations is introduced. browser.navigation_retries remains a required nonnegative integer, never a boolean, initially one, and bounds only automatic recovery of explicit navigate requests from acknowledged ordinary loading errors. Such retries repeat only the same requested public URL and each obeys current permissions and resolves current ordinary browser state. Blocked or stale error retries perform no new effect and return current observable page state with a nonfatal warning; exhausted loading errors also return incomplete current observations. Ordinary observed 404 or CAPTCHA content does not itself trigger fatal shutdown or an automatic reload based on text. Completed native download denial retains AG_005 successful enforcement semantics. A missing command acknowledgment, failed required ordinary inspection, lost or mismatched control, interruption and other machinery failures remain fatal. No recovery automatically repeats click, type, keypress, back or scroll, changes protections, replaces the browser or opens another execution route.

specs.title: Secret protection
specs.contract: Signal Scout evidence/audit/checkpoint/report storage accepts allowlisted fields only and passes persisted strings through Hermes secret redaction. It never stores raw tool arguments or raw tool results in the audit trail. Credentials, session tokens, cookies, authorization headers, and secret configuration values do not enter this application-managed evidence, checkpoint or report storage; stored failures retain only source ID and redacted failure class. Operational native diagnostics follow SR_003 instead of this stricter audit-storage boundary. No reviewer evidence pipeline is active; broader storage/audit handling remains distinct from ordinary in-memory observations. Broader storage/audit flow remains unimplemented.

specs.title: Scout-only authenticated accounts
specs.contract: A source requiring authentication can be enabled only through a dedicated Signal Scout account and isolated browser profile approved for that platform. Personal accounts and personal browser profiles are rejected.
specs.blocker: Scout-only accounts and platform-specific authentication policies have not been provisioned. Public-source browsing can proceed independently.

specs.title: Diagnosable ordinary browser-action failures
specs.contract: Unexpected browser-action failures emit best-effort native Python diagnostics through existing Hermes logging. At configured INFO level, records identify action, actual failed phase, monotonic elapsed time and underlying exception details/traceback when an exception exists. Failing CDP commands retain method, configured timeout, elapsed time, command/session/connection IDs, send/matching-response facts, protocol errors and selected navigation/dialog/detach/crash metadata. Distinguish missing command responses from initial-document observation deadlines. Unexpected inspection errors retain diagnostics before sanitized conversion. Native context, levels, rotation, persistence and secret redaction follow SR_003; redaction does not guarantee removal of every sensitive string. Do not add bulk arguments/results, page-body, screenshot or CDP payload dumps. Raw exceptions, traces and protocol payloads stay out of model-facing action results; AG_008 retains sanitized observed URL/readiness/deadline facts. Logging failure cannot replace the real result, execute an action or prevent required fatal closure. Preserve ordinary stale/blocked rejection, command/observation deadlines, bounded explicit-navigation loading-error retries, download/network protections and exact cleanup. No reviewer phase, verdict or review failure metadata remains; diagnostics do not claim to fix Chromium failures.

specs.title: Persistent browser-process and relay diagnostics
specs.contract: During an owned browser run, Chromium diagnostic output, launcher exceptions and observed child termination, and CDP relay connection failures or endings are collected through the trusted host and retained in the existing diagnostic log volume under configured verbosity, size and backup limits and native secret redaction. Records identify the run and component; relay records distinguish connections and direction with observed EOF, error or cancellation, and child records distinguish observed exit code or signal from requested shutdown. Browser output is drained during execution rather than only after failure so the diagnostic mechanism does not fill a pipe and stall Chromium. Bounded browser-output transport is permitted; the browser receives no persistent log/auth mount, Docker socket, added network permission or new model tool. Diagnostics preserve useful native error detail without adding bulk CDP/HTTP payload, screenshot, page-body, cookie, credential dumps. Native redaction is not universal removal of sensitive content. A broken diagnostic stream or sink attempts a visible diagnostic but does not replace the mission result, authorize an action or prevent existing owned cleanup. Collection is best effort, not a guarantee against host death, forced process kill, transport-buffer eviction or Docker unavailability. Browser actions, helper inactivity/reconnect behavior, existing timeouts and retries, browser/network/download protections and mission lifecycle outcomes remain unchanged.

specs.title: Owned browser failure state survives ordinary teardown
specs.contract: Before the trusted owner intentionally stops or removes its exact browser container on normal completion, handled failure, startup failure or cancellation, it attempts to persist a timestamped pre-teardown state observation identifying the run and verified full container ID and available Docker running/status, exit-code, OOMKilled and error fields. Observation before intentional stop remains distinguishable from post-stop state so cleanup-induced termination is not presented as the original failure. Already-exited containers are observed before removal when still inspectable; missing containers, unavailable process observations or failed inspection are reported as unavailable rather than invented crash causes. Chromium child status and Docker container status are separate observations; exit code 137 or SIGKILL alone is not labeled proof of OOM. Only relevant state fields are retained, not complete Docker inspection documents, environment, authentication or viewer secrets. State capture and final diagnostic collection are attempted while resources remain available but their failure does not block ordinary exact-owned cleanup or alter the mission outcome. Foreign containers and existing auth/log volumes remain untouched. No watchdog, restart, orphan adoption, retained crashed container or guarantee after host death is introduced, and observations do not assert the original mission failure has been diagnosed.

specs.title: Reviewer-free browser mission execution
specs.contract: Research startup and browser_scout actions operate without constructing a safety reviewer, requiring reviewer model/settings/policy, making auxiliary safety-model requests, preparing review evidence packets or comparing pre-approval and post-approval context. No toggle, always-approve reviewer or dormant reviewed execution path remains. Ordinary current-target resolution, stale-reference rejection, visibility and iframe coordinate handling, explicit screenshot support, truthful action outcomes and page observations remain available. No auxiliary safety model runs; existing main-model and context-management calls remain. Independent browser ownership, browser-only tool exposure, container/network/download protections and normal fatal-stop/cleanup boundaries remain. The previous committed reviewer is recoverable through the documented Git archive reference. Main-agent instructions guide research behavior but do not claim independent action-level adjudication. This retirement does not claim that shared Chromium/frame-observation failures have been fixed.
